'''''Bauhinia acuminata''''' is a [[species]] of flowering [[shrub]] native to tropical southeastern [[Asia]]. Common names include '''dwarf white bauhinia''', '''white orchid-tree''' and '''snowy orchid-tree'''.<ref name=pier>Pacific Island Ecosystems at Risk: [http://www.hear.org/Pier/species/bauhinia_acuminata.htm ''Bauhinia acuminata'']</ref> The exact native range is obscure due to extensive cultivation, but probably from [[Malaysia]], [[Indonesia]] ([[Java]], [[Borneo]], [[Kalimantan]], [[Lesser Sunda Islands]]), and the [[Philippines]].<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | access-date = 16 January 2018}}</ref>

It grows two to three meters tall. Like the other ''Bauhinia'' species, the [[leaf|leaves]] are bilobed, shaped like an [[ox]] [[hoof]]; they are {{convert|6|to|15|cm|in|frac=4}} long and broad, with the apical cleft up to {{convert|5|cm|in|0}} deep; the [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]] is {{convert|1.5|to|4|cm|in|frac=4}} long. The [[flowers]] are fragrant, {{convert|8|to|12|cm|in|frac=4}} in diameter, with five white petals, ten yellow-tipped [[stamen]]s and a green [[Gynoecium|stigma]]. The [[fruit]] is a [[legume|pod]] {{convert|7.5|to|15|cm|in|frac=4}} long and {{convert|1.5|to|1.8|cm|in|frac=4}} broad. The species occurs in [[deciduous forest]]s and scrub.<ref name=pier/><ref>Flowers of India: [http://www.flowersofindia.net/catalog/slides/White%20Orchid%20Tree.html White Orchid Tree]</ref><ref name=rhs>Huxley, A., ed. (1992). ''New RHS Dictionary of Gardening''. Macmillan {{ISBN|0-333-47494-5}}.</ref>

It is widely cultivated throughout the tropics as an [[ornamental plant]]. It may be found as an escape from cultivation in some areas, and has become [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] on the [[Cape York Peninsula]], [[Australia]].<ref name=pier/>

The plant has a number of [[Ethnobotany|ethnobotanical]] uses around the world. The roots are used by the Javanese to treat cough and cold and in India the leaves and bark are used to treat asthma.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NParks {{!}} Bauhinia acuminata|url=https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/3/6/3605|access-date=2022-02-14|website=www.nparks.gov.sg}}</ref> It is also used in many culinary dishes of [[Odisha]]
